anchors.seams: Each copy is solved on its own, so an area's outer faces are constrained ONLY by their sets. Pin them to single connectors wherever neighbouring copies must line up.
anchors.socketSets: A tile face carries ONE connector name. An anchor face carries a SET: a plain name ("rock") accepts exactly that connector, "h1|h2|h3" accepts any of the alternatives, and "*" accepts any connector. An anchor's candidates are the bag's tiles whose four faces its four sets accept.
anchors.solve: Game mode solves each area of each parallel copy AS A WHOLE: anchors that share a full edge (exactly one footprint apart) must agree on it, and the solver propagates that, collapses the most-constrained anchor first with a weighted random pick, and backtracks on a contradiction. Deterministic from the world seed, the copy and the area. An area with no consistent solution falls back (with a console warning) to per-anchor picks, and neighbours may then not join. The editor preview picks per anchor.
anchors.variety: Set talus:boundary on the area to pin its OUTER faces (a sky row on top, bedrock below, one fixed connector at both ends so copies join), and interiorSocket="*" or alternatives ("h1|h2|h3") on the import to let the solver vary the interior: elevation connectors (h1/h2/h3 = ground height at the tile edge) and ramp tiles joining a surface band to an underground band then produce a different map per copy.

area.boundary: talus:boundary (default "edge") is the socket SET given to faces on the rect's OUTER edge — that is what stops the wave. Interior faces get the import's interiorSocket (default "open"; "*" or "a|b" alternatives let the copy-wide solve choose — see anchors.variety).
area.how: <g class="wfc-area" talus:area="meadow"> containing a <rect>, or carrying talus:chunkX0/Y0/X1/Y1 directly. Every FULL footprint inside the rect becomes an anchor bound to that bag.
area.note: Anchors sit on the footprint grid, not on every chunk — a 4-chunk tile occupies four. A partial footprint at the far edge is DROPPED rather than clipped, because half a tile is not a tile; size the rect in whole footprints to avoid surprises.

batching: One import_wfc_tiles call carries up to 25 tiles. A bag of 100 is a handful of calls, not 100 — call plan_wfc_bag for the batches.
example:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:talus="https://talus.dev/ns/world" viewBox="0 0 768 256">
  <!-- three 4x4 tiles laid side by side; each declares where its own pixels are -->
  <!-- talus:element on the group; every child is made of it -->
  <g class="wfc-tile" talus:tile="ground" talus:area="meadow" talus:size="4x4"
     talus:origin="0 0" talus:sockets="grass grass grass grass" talus:weight="8">
    <rect x="0" y="128" width="256" height="128" talus:element="STONE"/>
  </g>
  <g class="wfc-tile" talus:tile="pond" talus:area="meadow" talus:size="4x4"
     talus:origin="256 0" talus:sockets="grass grass grass grass" talus:weight="1">
    <rect x="256" y="128" width="256" height="128" talus:element="STONE"/>
    <ellipse cx="384" cy="176" rx="70" ry="34" talus:element="WATER"/>
  </g>
  <g class="wfc-tile" talus:tile="cliff-e" talus:area="meadow" talus:size="4x4"
     talus:origin="512 0" talus:north="grass" talus:south="grass" talus:east="cliff" talus:west="grass">
    <rect x="512" y="64" width="256" height="192" talus:element="BASALT"/>
  </g>
  <!-- and where the bag gets used -->
  <g class="wfc-area" talus:area="meadow" talus:chunkX0="0" talus:chunkY0="0"
     talus:chunkX1="15" talus:chunkY1="15"/>
</svg>

Note "cliff" above appears only on an EAST face — bagProblems will say so, and the fix is a tile with
talus:west="cliff" for it to butt against.
matter: A tile is made of the same shapes as any other SVG matter, and the SAME RULE applies: name it with talus:element="STONE". A fill colour resolves only on an EXACT match to an element's own colour, so hand-picked hex (#55515a for rock, #24232b for backdrop) resolves to nothing and every shape falls back to one default element — the tiles still import, still report ok, and the whole cave comes out a single material. Check `report.unresolved` and `report.fallbackCells` on every import. Colour belongs in fill= only as a readable hint ALONGSIDE talus:element. See describe_svg_contract for the full vocabulary.
summary: A WFC tile is a NODE in an adjacency graph and its four sockets are the EDGES. Two tiles may sit side by side exactly when the facing socket names are EQUAL — plain string equality, no other rule. An AREA is a BAG: the solver only picks tiles whose area matches the anchor's, so two areas never contaminate each other even if they share socket names. An ANCHOR (one tile slot of an area) says which connectors each of its faces ACCEPTS, and in the game every anchor of an area is solved together so neighbours always agree — see anchors.
theOneRule: A socket name you use on a NORTH face must be used by some tile on a SOUTH face, and EAST must be matched by WEST. A name that appears on only one side can never get a neighbour there — the wave dead-ends and the map comes out with a hole. import_wfc_tiles reports this as `bagProblems`; it is the single most common way a WFC palette fails, and it fails as a MAP, not as an error. "edge" is exempt: it is the convention for a face that ends the wave.

attributes.talus:area: The bag. REQUIRED — a tile with no area can never be picked.
attributes.talus:origin: "x y" — the top-left of this tile's content in document pixels. Give each tile its own origin so their pixels do not overlap; a strip or grid inside the document is the natural layout.
attributes.talus:rotate: "90 180 270" — which rotations the solver may also use.
attributes.talus:size: "WxH" in CHUNKS. ALWAYS SET IT to the size you drew — 4x4 = a 256x256 px tile, the usual footprint. Omitting it falls back to the import's tileSizeChunks, and if that is wrong too the tile becomes a CROP of your art (only its top-left chunk) with no error; the import reports that as an issue saying matter was dropped.
attributes.talus:sockets: "north south east west" in that order. Or use talus:north / talus:south / talus:east / talus:west individually. Unstated faces default to "edge".
attributes.talus:tags: Free text carried onto the tile row.
attributes.talus:tile: Node name. Unique in the document; re-importing the same name updates that tile.
attributes.talus:weight: Relative pick likelihood in the bag (default 1). Weight common ground high and features low, or the map reads as noise.

tile.how: <g class="wfc-tile" ...> whose CHILD SHAPES are the tile's content, drawn in the same world pixels as any other SVG matter. The shapes also paint the document, which is what lets you SEE your palette. Paint inherits: <g talus:element="STONE"> gives every child that element unless the child names its own.
